steps.title: One property, three consequences
steps.html:
Whether a noun is countable in English is not a fact about the world; it is a fact about the word. Once you know it, three things follow automatically.

The plural. Countable nouns have one; uncountable nouns do not. Two communities, but never two researches. The article. A singular countable noun must have one: a community, the community. An uncountable noun takes none when it is general, and the when it is specific: support is free, but the support she got was excellent. The quantifier. Many, a few and several go with countable nouns; much, a little and a great deal of go with uncountable ones.

steps.title: The words that catch learners out
steps.html:
• Uncountable in English, countable in many other languages: research, advice, information, equipment, furniture, permission, support, homework, news, progress.
  • To count them, use a unit word: a piece of research, a word of advice, an item of equipment.
  • The verb is singular: research suggests, the news is, this information is.
  • Some nouns are both, with different meanings: a paper (an article) and paper (the material); a coffee (a cup) and coffee (the drink); an experience (an event) and experience (what you have learned).

steps.title: Напиши свой текст
steps.sub: Напиши ответ, затем сверься с образцом
steps.modelHtml:
We propose an online community for carers — the people who look after a parent or a husband or wife at home, full time and mostly alone. There are, according to recent research, about four hundred of them in this town, and hardly any support available to them locally.

The group would do three things. It would let members ask practical questions at two in the morning, which is when most of them are awake. It would carry a list of what is available in the district, since a great deal of that information exists and almost none of it is in one place. And it would organise one meeting a month in the library itself, for anybody who can get out of the house.

It needs very little equipment and no permission from anybody. It needs one moderator, paid for four hours a week, and somebody who will not lose interest in the second year. That, rather than the technology, is what such groups usually fail on. Membership elsewhere has grown noticeably wherever a paid moderator was kept.
